rv.q: In a play that has all the drama of a Wikipedia entry, we learn that it was thanks to an affair with President John F Kennedy, and later with his brother Bobby, that Marilyn was murdered.
But the script has wings of lead. Not once does it take off as an involving drama.
Only the most devoted fans will get excited by these stubbornly spark-free two hours at London's Emerald Theatre.
There is little to gain from this trot through Monroe's life, narrated in cliches.
The only mystery here is how this comically inept conspiracy theory drama ever made it to the London stage.
Unfortunately our online content management system does not allow for zero-star reviews. If it did, this would be my first.
This isn't just bad theatre; it's toe-curlingly crass and ethically grubby. Avoid.
Originally a movie theatre and later a music venue and cabaret space, Dita Von Teese, The Psychedelic Furs, Motorhead and Pearl Jam have all performed here.
This clunky idea makes the show visually unpleasant.
Unfortunately, new play Who Killed Marilyn? falls hard into the latter.
If ChatGPT were commissioned to write a play about Marilyn Monroe, it would probably look a lot like this.
